11.31.4.en: This person, who walks by his own will, places himself above everything like Lucifer (Isa 14:13-14), even above God Himself. He represents the glorification of the self, which the Christian faith resists.

11.31.5.en: He ascribes to himself divine honors and utters wonders (blasphemies) against God, the God of gods. Since it is said that he regards not the God of his fathers, some have been led to say that the Antichrist will be a Jew who renounces the faith.

11.31.6.en: What is stated here about the Antichrist, that he is a ruler who restores the Roman state and that he resists the Jews, has made some think that he is a Christian who renounces the faith.

11.31.7.en: The Hebrew word for "the God of his fathers" is Elohim, which is also translated "gods"; thus it is thought that he despises all the religions of his fathers. The only god he believes in is power and violence, the god of military might.

11.31.8.en: As for "the desire of women", as St. Jerome says: [There are two interpretations of this expression: either that it means seeking the desire of women or renouncing this desire, as the Antichrist will do, who will pretend to chastity in order to deceive many. Some see that it refers here to the desire of Jewish women to conceive the Messiah. And perhaps it means that he cares nothing for women and their desires. It is said that Hitler was of this kind. In the sixteenth century there were two opinions, which Calvin rejected; the first is that what is meant here is "the Pope", for in chapter seven of the first volume of the Councils the canons of Pope Siricius say that those who are in the flesh cannot please God, reckoning that marriage is close to fornication. The second opinion is the desire for women, where a person is permitted to be joined legally to more than one wife. And some see that the talk here is about the Roman emperors who were famous for their hatred of their wives and of the female sex in general.

11.31.9.en: St. Jerome says: [The text here applies to the Antichrist and not to Antiochus, because the latter tried to compel the Jews and the Samaritans to keep feasts for his gods, and he set up statues of the Greek gods; but the Antichrist cares nothing for the gods of his fathers, but sets himself up as God.

11.31.10.en: "But in his estate shall he honour the God of forces: and a god whom his fathers knew not shall he honour with gold, and silver, and with precious stones, and pleasant things.

11.31.11.en: Thus shall he do in the most strong holds with a strange god:

11.32.0.en: whoso knoweth him he shall increase with glory, and he shall cause them to rule over many, and shall divide the land for a reward" [38-39].

11.32.1.en: He speaks here about the "Antichrist", the god whom his fathers knew not, and he means "himself", for he ascribes to himself divine honors, and demands all wealth and authority for himself; he is the strange god. And he will give gifts to those who submit to him and are deceived by him.

11.32.2.en: Some see that this applies also to the Roman state, which rejected the worship of the living God, and whose god was power and impregnable fortresses, and the love of authority along with the demanding of tribute and material gains from the states it colonized. The emperors set up for themselves or for their gods statues of gold, silver, precious stones, and costly things. They reckoned themselves greater and stronger than the gods, so that none could reach them. They also looked to "Rome" as the god who must be honored above all the gods.

11.32.3.en: The Greeks did not dare to attack the gods, whichever they were, but the Romans often pretended to honor even the strange gods of other peoples, yet they also mocked the gods and proclaimed their denial, reckoning that their state and their entity stood above every consideration.

11.32.4.en: "And at the time of the end shall the king of the south push at him: and the king of the north shall rise up against him with chariots, and with horsemen, and with many ships; and he shall enter into the countries, and shall overflow and pass through.

11.32.5.en: He shall enter also into the glorious land, and many shall stumble: but these shall escape out of his hand, even Edom, and Moab, and the chief of the children of Ammon.

11.32.6.en: He shall stretch forth his hand also upon the countries: and the land of Egypt shall not escape.

11.32.7.en: But he shall have power over the treasures of gold and of silver, and over all the precious things of Egypt:

11.32.8.en: and the Libyans and the Ethiopians shall be at his steps.

11.32.9.en: But tidings out of the east and out of the north shall trouble him: therefore he shall go forth with great fury to destroy, and utterly to make away many.

11.33.0.en: And he shall plant the tabernacles of his palace between the seas and the glorious holy mountain; yet he shall come to his end, and none shall help him" [40-45]. [40-45] presents to us some events of the last days of the self-exalting king and others.

11.33.1.en: It is noted that it presents to us three persons: 1. The self-exalting king, "the Antichrist". 2. The king of the south (Egypt). 3. The king of the north (Syria).

11.33.2.en: St. Jerome says: [We read that Antiochus fulfilled this in part, but when we note what follows in detail, "and the Libyans (Libyans) and the Ethiopians (Ethiopians) shall be at his steps", our school insists that this suits the Antichrist more. For Antiochus never conquered Libya, which most writers understand as North Africa, nor Ethiopia].

11.34.0.en: The Antichrist will set up his headquarters in Jerusalem, and his dominion will extend to the seas [45], especially the Mediterranean Sea and the Dead Sea. He will set up his headquarters on the glorious holy mountain, that is, Mount Zion. And with all the power and authority he attains, no one will be able to support him; the Antichrist will collapse before Elijah and Enoch, who support the Church in his time and prepare the believers for the final coming of the Lord Christ.

11.34.1.en: St. Jerome says: [Our school of thought insists that the Antichrist will perish at the very place where the Lord ascended to heaven (the Mount of Olives)].

11.34.2.en: Let history pass, and let the last times come!

11.34.3.en: * All history is in Your grasp, and nothing is hidden from You.

11.34.4.en: Mighty men arise and others collapse.

11.34.5.en: Covenants are made, some keep them, and others break them.

11.34.6.en: Kingdom wrestles with kingdom, and history folds up this one and that.

11.34.7.en: * Let history pass and be folded up with all its events, and let the last times come.

11.34.8.en: The Antichrist will pour out all his poisons; but our victorious Christ is surely coming!

11.34.9.en: Come, O Victor, and let Your believers be glorified!

12.0.0.en: 1 And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time:

12.0.1.en: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book. [1].

12.0.2.en: Since the chapter opens with the expression "And at that time" [1], it is clear that it continues what is stated in the previous chapter. For at the peak of the Antichrist's power the archangel Michael arises and works on behalf of the Church [as it is written in (Rev 12)], and this is in the period of the great tribulation that the Lord Christ announces (Mt 24:15-22).

12.0.3.en: In the midst of the tribulation God delivers the people of Daniel, that is, the Church of the believers whose names are written in the book of life. It is constantly exposed to tribulation, but it is not forgotten before God; rather, the more the tribulation intensifies, the more God shows His care for it. It is in the hand of its Savior the Lord Christ, who works for its building up, and uses His angels and archangels to protect it.

12.1.0.en: 2 And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt. 3 And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever. [2-3].

12.2.0.en: Some consider the Book of Daniel to be the first book of the Old Testament to speak clearly and strongly about the resurrection and to determine its time. When the great day of the Lord comes, the wise who obeyed God will shine like eternal stars. Yet this matter was reckoned beyond the ability of Daniel himself, for he says: "And I heard, but I understood not" [8].

12.2.1.en: Some try to distinguish here between two resurrections, one for the millennial reign and the other for eternal life, but it is clear that the talk here is of one resurrection and an eternal judgment, and eternal glory or torment.

12.2.2.en: * But those lords and teachers who have knowledge of the Law will shine like the heaven, and those who urge the peoples that lag behind in faith to give heed to the worship of God will glitter like stars in eternity.

12.2.3.en: St. Jerome * Let us flee with all our strength from the hindrances of this world and seek some hours in which we can devote ourselves to prayer or the reading of the Holy Bible for the salvation of our souls. This fulfills in us what is written: "And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament".

12.2.4.en: Fr. Caesarius * After the Antichrist is shattered and destroyed by the breath of the Savior's mouth, the people written in the book of God will be saved, each according to his merit; some will arise to everlasting life, and others to everlasting shame.

12.2.5.en: Teachers are likened to the very heavens, and those who teach others are compared to the brightness of the stars. For it is not enough for a person to know wisdom, but it is fitting for him to teach it to others.

12.2.6.en: The tongue of teaching that remains silent and edifies no one receives no reward.

12.2.7.en: St. Jerome * The Lord helps the humble, and the humble are changed into stars. For "the righteous shall shine as the stars", as Daniel says.

12.3.0.en: 4 But thou, O Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end: many shall peruse it, and knowledge shall be increased. 5 Then I Daniel looked, and, behold, there stood other two, the one on this side of the bank of the river, and the other on that side of the bank of the river. 6 And one said to the man clothed in linen, which was upon the waters of the river, How long shall it be to the end of these wonders? 7 And I heard the man clothed in linen, which was upon the waters of the river, when he held up his right hand and his left hand unto heaven, and sware by him that liveth for ever that it shall be for a time, and two times, and an half; and when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished. 8 And I heard, but I understood not: then said I, O my Lord, what shall be the end of these things? 9 And he said, Go thy way, Daniel: for the words are closed up and sealed till the time of the end. 10 Many shall be purified, and made white, and tried; but the wicked shall do wickedly: and none of the wicked shall understand; but the wise shall understand. 11 And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days. 12 Blessed is he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days. 13 But go thou thy way till the end be: for thou shalt rest, and stand in thy lot at the end of the days.

12.3.1.en: "But thou, O Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end:

12.3.2.en: many shall peruse it, and knowledge shall be increased" [4].

12.3.3.en: Daniel was commanded to seal the book, even "to the time of the end", but knowledge shall be increased, although a person remains as in a riddle until what is stated in the book is fully realized. Perhaps by the sealing here is meant that the prophecies remain unclear until salvation is accomplished in the fullness of the times, and the mysteries of the Second Coming are uncovered as in the Book of Revelation (Rev 22:10). For this reason many scholars see that the Book of Revelation is the key to the Book of Daniel.

12.3.4.en: St. Irenaeus sees that the divine inspiration asked Daniel to seal the prophecy, because no one could grasp it until the Lord Christ came, who is the goal of the prophecies, and then the believers would grasp its mystery, for he says: [The treasure hidden in the Holy Scriptures is Christ, to whom reference is made through types and parables. And since His human nature could not be understood before these predicted things were fulfilled, that is, before the coming of Christ, therefore it was said to Daniel the prophet: "Shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end, that many may learn and knowledge be perfected. At that time, when the dispensation is accomplished, they shall know all these things" (cf. Dan 12:4, 7). For every prophecy, before its fulfillment, is a riddle and an obscurity to men. But when the time comes and the prophecies are fulfilled, they become clear and their interpretation becomes certain].

12.3.5.en: St. Hippolytus of Rome says: [The things that were spoken in ancient times through the Law and the Prophets were all sealed, and were not known to men; Isaiah declares this by saying: "the sealed book, which men deliver to one that is learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he saith, I cannot; for it is sealed" (Isa 29:11). It is fitting and necessary that the things spoken by the prophets in ancient times should be sealed to the unbelieving Pharisees, who thought they understood the letter of the Law, while they are unsealed to the believers. The ancient things were sealed, but now by the grace of the Lord God all of them are unsealed to the saints. For He Himself (God) was the seal and the Church is the key: "he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth", as John says (Rev 3:7)... For this reason the angel says to Daniel: "Seal the words, for the vision is until the time of the end". But of Christ it is not said "seal", but rather He loosed the things that had been bound in ancient times, that by His grace the will of the Father may be known, and we may believe in Him whom He sent for the salvation of men, our Lord Jesus].

12.3.6.en: St. Jerome says [He who declared the truth in many ways to Daniel declares that the things He said are secret. And He asked him to roll up the scroll containing His words, and to put a seal on the book. The result is that many read it and ask about its fulfillment through history, and differ in their opinions (interpretations) because of its great obscurity.

12.3.7.en: By saying "many shall peruse it" [4], or "pass through it", he indicates that many read it...

12.3.8.en: And also in the Revelation of John a book is seen sealed within and without. And since no one could be found worthy to loose its seals, John says: "And I wept much... and a voice came to me: Weep not much, behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seals thereof" (cf. Rev 5:4).

12.3.9.en: But that book can be opened by one who learns the mysteries of the Scripture and understands its hidden truths and its words that seem dark because of the greatness of the mysteries they contain. It is he who is able to explain the parables and to turn the letter that kills into the Spirit that gives life.

12.3.10.en: St. Jerome "Then I Daniel looked, and, behold, there stood other two, the one on this side of the bank of the river, and the other on that side of the bank of the river.

12.3.11.en: And one said to the man clothed in linen, which was upon the waters of the river,

12.3.12.en: How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?

12.3.13.en: And I heard the man clothed in linen, which was upon the waters of the river, when he held up his right hand and his left hand unto heaven, and sware by him that liveth for ever that it shall be for a time, and two times, and an half.

12.3.14.en: And when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished.

12.3.15.en: And I heard, but I understood not: then said I, O my Lord, what shall be the end of these things?

12.3.16.en: And he said, Go thy way, Daniel: for the words are closed up and sealed till the time of the end.

12.3.17.en: Many shall be purified, and made white, and tried;

12.4.0.en: but the wicked shall do wickedly: and none of the wicked shall understand; but the wise shall understand" [5-10].

12.4.1.en: In order that Daniel might seal the book, he saw two other angels and the one clothed in linen, that is, the Word of God before the Incarnation (Dan 6:10). One of the angels asked him about the duration of this tribulation, and the answer came: for a time, and two times, and a half, that is, three and a half years. This is half of the week of which Daniel spoke before, a period of very bitter persecution, ending with the breaking of the covenant of the predatory king. St. Jerome says: [The time, and two times, and a half cannot be meant as the three and a half years in which Antiochus defiled the Temple, as Porphyry claimed, because this would require that the victor enjoy an eternal kingdom, and that all the kings submit to him and obey him, and this did not happen. Rather it is clear that the talk here is about the Antichrist, who reigns for 1290 days or three and a half years.

12.5.0.en: Although Daniel was asked to seal the book, because it contains mysteries that not everyone knows, and although Daniel himself says: "And I heard, but I understood not" [8], yet at the same time he affirms that whoever is pure and sanctified will understand what was said and become wise, while the wicked will not understand. Knowledge and wisdom here are relative matters; without doubt Daniel perceived much of the mysteries of the end of the age, but as in a mirror, or through the shadow, yet knowledge increases for the believers and many things are uncovered.

12.5.1.en: * He remarked that when the end comes the wicked will lack understanding, while those instructed in the teachings of God will be able to understand. For wisdom will not enter a perverse soul, nor can it disclose itself to a body subject to sins.

12.5.2.en: St. Jerome "And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days.

12.6.0.en: Blessed is he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days" [11-12].

12.6.1.en: He determines the period in days and not years, 1290 days, which means three and a half years, in which the Church suffers severe tribulation, with 45 days added to it (1335 days), and perhaps this period is the one between the killing of the Antichrist and the coming of the Lord Christ. It is a period of rest for the one who was led astray after the Antichrist to return and repent, and at the same time a period of purification for the believers, who await with joy the coming of Christ after deliverance from the Antichrist. Therefore Daniel the prophet pronounces blessed him that waiteth and cometh to the 1335 days.

12.6.2.en: St. Jerome says: [It is clear that the three and a half years were accepted with regard to the time of the Antichrist, for he will persecute the saints for three and a half years or 1290 days, and then he will face his fall on the famous holy mountain. Thus from the time at which he prevents the Endelekismos, which is translated "the perpetual sacrifice", that is, from the time at which the Antichrist reigns over the world and prevents the worship of God until the day of his death, the three and a half years or the 1290 days are completed].

12.6.3.en: * By this he means that blessed is he who waits forty-five days after the specified number (1290), for in this period our Lord will come in His glory. But the reason for the forty-five days after the killing of the Antichrist is a matter settled in the knowledge of God, unless we say that the judgment of the saints is postponed so that their faith may be tested. (by the final coming of Christ).

12.7.0.en: St. Jerome "But go thou thy way till the end be: for thou shalt rest, and stand in thy lot at the end of the days" [13].

12.7.1.en: Finally he asks Daniel to rest until he arises when the Lord of glory comes, who says, "Behold, I come quickly" (Rev 22).

12.7.2.en: * From this remark it appears clearly that the whole text of the prophecy concerns the resurrection of all the dead, the time at which the prophet too will arise.

12.7.3.en: St. Jerome In the sixteenth century John Calvin says that some commentators add the two numbers together (1290 + 1335), making about 2600 years, and since the prophecy dates from about 600 BC, the coming of the Lord Christ with the end of the world would be 2000 years after His first coming. Calvin rejected this interpretation.

12.7.4.en: And some comment on the saying of the Lord Christ in the parable of "the Good Samaritan": "And on the morrow when he departed, he took out two pence, and gave them to the host, and said unto him, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee" (Lk 10:35), using the symbolic interpretation, that the Lord Christ has entrusted the wounded souls in this world into the hands of the militant Church for a period of 2000 years. For one day with the Lord is as a thousand years, so the two pence represent two thousand years after the ministry of Christ, that is, the Lord Christ returns, as it were, to the inn at the beginning of the twenty-first century.

12.7.5.en: His Grace Anba Dioscorus presented a study on the Book of Daniel in which he reveals the nearness of the end of the world, and opinions have also appeared in the West supporting the speedy end of the world. Some scientists have also seen that the widening of the ozone hole, from the scientific side, caused the movement of a huge mass of ice in the South Pole region over a distance of about 3 kilometers, and that its movement at this rate will lead to an imbalance in the magnetism and equilibrium of the earth, causing strong earthquakes and volcanoes that end in the destruction of the earth a few years after the year 2000.

12.7.6.en: The appearance of these opinions had strong repercussions in the East and the West, between supporters and opponents. But without doubt, when the "Antichrist" appears, the believers will discover that what is stated in the Book of Daniel was quite clear to the pious, just as the Church of the New Testament realized from the beginning of its launch, with the pious among the Jews, that the times relating to the coming of Christ were explicit and clear.

12.7.7.en: What I wish to make clear here is that since the Ascension of the Lord Christ the Church has been joyfully awaiting His quick coming, in the certainty that He is coming, and coming quickly, yet without disregard for temporal obligations and without slackness. The Lord Christ revealed to her the sure signs of His coming so that she might prepare with patience and face the tribulations, especially the great tribulation and His abomination of desolation, and also prepare with joy and hope that she has a share with Him in the Father's embrace. But now many think that awaiting the coming of the Lord Christ is regarded as a gloomy, pessimistic outlook that leads to slackness and negligence in fulfilling responsibilities; this reveals weakness of faith and the lack of hearts being kindled by the eschatological, heavenly thought.

12.7.8.en: He is surely coming! And the times will pass swiftly, and we will rejoice and exult in our resurrection with the dead, and our meeting with Him on the clouds.

12.7.9.en: Yes! Let the times pass away!

12.7.10.en: * For our sake You created time that we might glorify You in it, and for our sake time passes away that we might be glorified with You eternally.

12.7.11.en: Yes! Let the times pass away!

12.7.12.en: Come, O Beloved, to us, or carry us by Your Holy Spirit to You; we are hastening to meet You!

12.7.13.en: * Open the eyes of our hearts, that we may see You coming now into our depths, and see our souls passing over to You, enjoying Your presence!
